content.text:
Confirmed [#1411](https://github.com/jdx/usage/issues/1411): this is an intentional limitation of current routing, and the proposed opt-in makes sense.

Using a minimal `em` command with default `install`, I reproduced:

| Input | Current behavior |
|---|---|
| `em firefox` | Routes to `install` |
| `em -ua @world` | Rejects `-ua` |
| `em install -ua @world` | Parses successfully |
| `em -r` | Rejects the flag |
| `em -p` | Stays on the parent |

The cause exists in both parsers:

- [usage-argv](/Users/jdx/src/usage/argv/src/lib.rs:2326) explicitly limits default routing to words. Flag parsing happens first.
- [usage-lib](/Users/jdx/src/usage/lib/src/parse.rs:1569) stops command discovery at an unknown flag, before reaching the default fallback.

I’d support `default_subcommand_flags`, disabled by default, with a lookahead before binding tokens. Simply retrying unknown flags against the default would miss the requested sibling precedence.

The implementation needs explicit handling for flag values that resemble sibling names, short bundles, `--`, help, and conflicting parent/default flag definitions. It must also preserve parent-owned prefix flags: `em -p firefox` already works.

This spans both parsers, derive/spec metadata, generators, and completion behavior. I reproduced the runtime failure against current source; no repository changes or GitHub comments were made.

The proposal lets a CLI omit its default subcommand even when flags come first.

Suppose `em` defaults to `install`, which owns `-u` and `-a`. Today:

```sh
em firefox             # means: em install firefox
em -ua @world          # errors: em doesn't recognize -u
```

With `default_subcommand_flags` enabled, the second command would mean `em install -ua @world`.

To choose the command, the parser would first look ahead through the arguments, skipping recognized flags **and their values**:

- If the first remaining word names a sibling, such as `query`, keep normal explicit-subcommand parsing.
- If there are only parent flags, such as `--help` or `-p`, stay on the parent.
- If there’s an ordinary argument like `firefox`, or a default-command flag like `-r` with no sibling selector, select the default.

That lookahead chooses the command before flags get bound. It doesn’t make default-command flags valid everywhere: `em -u query` would still follow today’s parsing rules and could reject `-u`.

The behavior would be opt-in because some CLIs rely on rejecting child-only flags before the subcommand. Existing `default_subcommand` behavior would remain unchanged unless they enable it.
make a pr, post a reply
I’ll implement the opt-in routing, add regression coverage, and open a ready-for-review PR. Then I’ll reply to #1411 with the behavior and PR link.
